mn118:1.2: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, together with several well-known senior disciples, such as
mn118:1.3: the venerables Sāriputta, Mahāmoggallāna, Mahākassapa, Mahākaccāna, Mahākoṭṭhita, Mahākappina, Mahācunda, Anuruddha, Revata, Ānanda, and others.
mn118:2.1: Now at that time the senior bhikkhus were advising and instructing the junior bhikkhus.
mn118:2.2: Some senior bhikkhus instructed ten bhikkhus, while some instructed twenty, thirty, or forty.
mn118:2.3: Being instructed by the senior bhikkhus, the junior bhikkhus realized a higher distinction than they had before.
mn118:3.1: Now, at that time it was the sabbath—the full moon on the fifteenth day—and the Buddha was sitting surrounded by a Saṅgha of monks for the invitation to admonish.
mn118:3.2: Then the Buddha looked around the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, who were so very silent. He addressed them:
mn118:4.1: “I am satisfied, bhikkhus, with this practice.
mn118:4.2: My heart is satisfied with this practice.
mn118:4.3: So you should rouse up even more energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
mn118:4.4: I will wait here in Sāvatthī for the Komudī full moon of the fourth month.”
mn118:5.1: Bhikkhus from around the country heard about this,
mn118:5.3: and came down to Sāvatthī to see the Buddha.
mn118:6.1: And those senior bhikkhus instructed the junior bhikkhus even more.
mn118:6.2: Some senior bhikkhus instructed ten bhikkhus, while some instructed twenty, thirty, or forty.
mn118:6.3: Being instructed by the senior bhikkhus, the junior bhikkhus realized a higher distinction than they had before.
mn118:7.1: Now, at that time it was the sabbath—the Komudī full moon on the fifteenth day of the fourth month—and the Buddha was sitting in the open surrounded by a Saṅgha of monks.
mn118:7.2: Then the Buddha looked around the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, who were so very silent. He addressed them:
mn118:8.1: “This assembly has no chaff, bhikkhus, it is free of chaff, pure, and consolidated in the core.
mn118:8.2: Such is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus, such is this assembly!
mn118:8.3: An assembly such as this is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
mn118:8.4: Such is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus, such is this assembly!
mn118:8.5: For an assembly such as this, giving little becomes much, while giving much becomes even more.
mn118:8.6: Such is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus, such is this assembly!
mn118:8.7: An assembly such as this is rarely seen in the world.
mn118:8.8: Such is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus, such is this assembly!
mn118:8.9: An assembly such as this is worth traveling many leagues to see, even if you have to carry your own provisions in a knapsack.
mn118:9.1: For in this Saṅgha there are perfected bhikkhus, who have ended the defilements, completed the spiritual journey, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, achieved their heart’s goal, utterly ended the fetter of continued existence, and are rightly freed through enlightenment.
mn118:9.2: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:10.1: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who, with the ending of the five lower fetters are reborn spontaneously. They are extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
mn118:10.2: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:11.1: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.
mn118:11.2: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:12.1: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who, with the ending of three fetters are stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
mn118:12.2: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:13.1: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who are committed to developing the four kinds of mindfulness meditation …
mn118:14.2: the four bases of psychic power …
mn118:14.7: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:14.8: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who are committed to developing the meditation on love …
mn118:14.14: There are such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha.
mn118:14.15: In this Saṅgha there are bhikkhus who are committed to developing the meditation on mindfulness of breathing.
mn118:15.1: Bhikkhus, when mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated it is very fruitful and beneficial.
mn118:15.2: Mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
mn118:15.3: The four kinds of mindfulness meditation, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven awakening factors.
mn118:15.4: And the seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and freedom.
mn118:16.1: And how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated to be very fruitful and beneficial?
mn118:17.1: It’s when a bhikkhu—gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut—sits down cross-legged, sets their body straight, and brings mindfulness to the present.
mn118:17.2: Just mindful, he breathes in. Just mindful, he breathes out.
mn118:18.1: Breathing in long he knows: "I"m breathing in long." Breathing out long he knows: "I"m breathing out long."
mn118:18.2: Breathing in short he knows: "I"m breathing in short." Breathing out short he knows: "I"m breathing out short."
mn118:18.3: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in aware of the whole body." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out aware of the whole body."
mn118:18.4: He practices like this: "I"ll breathe in calming the body formations." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out calming the body formations."
mn118:19.1: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in feeling delighted." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out feeling delighted."
mn118:19.2: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in feeling contented." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out feeling contented."
mn118:19.3: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in experiencing the mental activity." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out experiencing the mental activity."
mn118:19.4: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in stilling the mental activity." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out stilling the mental activity."
mn118:20.1: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in experiencing the mind." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out experiencing the mind."
mn118:20.2: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in gladdening the mind." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out gladdening the mind."
mn118:20.3: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in collecting the mind." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out collecting the mind."
mn118:20.4: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in freeing the mind." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out freeing the mind."
mn118:21.1: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in observing impermanence." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out observing impermanence."
mn118:21.2: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in observing disinvolvement." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out observing disinvolvement."
mn118:21.3: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in observing cessation." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out observing cessation."
mn118:21.4: He practices like this: "I'll breathe in letting go." He practices like this: "I"ll breathe out letting go."
mn118:22.1: Mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated in this way, is very fruitful and beneficial.
mn118:23.1: And how is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?
mn118:24.1: Whenever a bhikkhu knows that they are breathing in long, or breathing out long,
mn118:24.2: or breathing in short, or breathing out short,
mn118:24.3: or being aware of the whole body,
mn118:24.5: at that time they’re meditating by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:24.6: For I say that the in-breaths and out-breaths are an aspect of the body.
mn118:24.7: That’s why at that time a bhikkhu is meditating by observing an aspect of the body—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:25.1: Whenever a bhikkhu practices breathing while feeling delighted,
mn118:25.5: at that time they meditate observing an aspect of feelings—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:25.6: For I say that careful attention to the in-breaths and out-breaths is an aspect of feelings.
mn118:25.7: That’s why at that time a bhikkhu is meditating by observing an aspect of feelings—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:26.1: Whenever a bhikkhu practices breathing while experiencing the mind,
mn118:26.5: at that time they meditate observing an aspect of mind—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:26.6: There is no development of mindfulness of breathing for someone who is unaware and lacks understanding, I say.
mn118:26.7: That’s why at that time a bhikkhu is meditating by observing an aspect of mind—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:27.1: Whenever a bhikkhu practices breathing while observing impermanence,
mn118:27.5: at that time they meditate observing an aspect of principles—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:27.6: Having seen with wisdom the giving up of craving and aversion, they watch over closely with equanimity.
mn118:27.7: That’s why at that time a bhikkhu is meditating by observing an aspect of principles—ardently aware and comprehending, letting go of craving and aversion towards the world.
mn118:28.1: That’s how mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.
mn118:29.1: And how are the four kinds of mindfulness meditation developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the seven awakening factors?
mn118:30.1: Whenever a bhikkhu meditates by observing an aspect of the body, at that time their awareness is established and lucid.
mn118:30.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of mindfulness; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:31.1: As they live mindfully in this way they investigate, explore, and inquire into that principle with wisdom.
mn118:31.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of investigation of principles; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:32.1: As they investigate principles with wisdom in this way their energy is roused up and unflagging.
mn118:32.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of energy; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:33.1: When they’re energetic, delight not of the flesh arises.
mn118:33.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of joy; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:34.1: When they're delighted, the body and mind become tranquil.
mn118:34.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of tranquility; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:35.1: When the body is calm and they feel contented, the mind becomes collected.
mn118:35.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of concentration; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:36.1: They closely watch over that collected mind.
mn118:36.2: At such a time, a bhikkhu cultivates the awakening factor of equanimity; they develop it and perfect it.
mn118:37.1: Whenever a bhikkhu meditates by observing feelings …
mn118:38.2: principles, at that time their awareness is established and lucid.
mn118:38.3: At such a time, a bhikkhu has initiated the awakening factor of mindfulness …
mn118:40.1: That’s how the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven awakening factors.
mn118:41.1: And how are the seven awakening factors developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and freedom?
mn118:42.1: It’s when a bhikkhu develops the awakening factors of mindfulness,
mn118:42.7: and equanimity, which rely on seclusion, disinvolvment, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.
mn118:43.1: That’s how the seven awakening factors, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and freedom.”
mn118:43.2: That is what the Buddha said.
mn118:43.3: Satisfied, the bhikkhus approved what the Buddha said.
